item.text: {"analysis":"The gated-history trial achieved host validation macro HR@10 of 0.5037, improving on the supplied previous result of 0.4975 by 0.0062 but remaining 0.0013 below the 0.505 baseline. Per-category HR@10 was 0.550 Movies_and_TV, 0.535 Industrial_and_Scientific, 0.380 Electronics, and 0.550 CDs_and_Vinyl. Electronics remains the weakest category. The result supports retaining causal history pooling as a candidate representation, but does not establish that broader history access caused the gain or that the approach exceeds baseline. Prior per-category numbers were not supplied, so category-level improvements cannot be quantified. Execution and host evaluation succeeded; no test results are reported.","code_summary":"One independently trained SASRec per category uses shared 96-dimensional item embeddings, two causal Transformer blocks with two heads, and a jointly trained history-attention branch. A learned query attends over nonpadding items in each causal prefix; projected pooled embeddings blend with Transformer features through an elementwise sigmoid gate initialized with zero weights and bias 2. Features pass through final layer normalization and L2 normalization, then score normalized item embeddings using a learned scale and jointly trained item bias. Training retains 256 sampled negatives, training-history exclusion, sampled-softmax loss, recency-weighted transitions, prefix augmentation, and AdamW. Checks cover finite pooled features and initial gradients, causal invariance, and checkpoint reload parity. The predictor strictly loads exactly one selected checkpoint per category, including all history-branch parameters; there is no averaging or auxiliary fitted scorer."}
